To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the four proton-hole nucleus 204Pt is populated by fragmentation of a 208Pb beam.
the structure of the magic Pt-204 nucleus can be understood within a simple spherical shell model and the two-body interaction that determines its structure has been revised.

the yrast structure of the four proton-hole nucleus 204Pt has been observed up the spin I = 10, the yrast states have half-lives ranging from 5.5 mu s to 146 ns, the structure of the magic nucleus 204Pt is well described in the framework of spherical shell model, and the two-body interaction between protons and neutrons for N=126, Z <82 has been revised.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structure of the heaviest nuclei and its evolution with neutron number, and with the structure of nuclei far from stability.
the study of the evolution of nuclear shell structure and its impact on nuclear structure, astrophysical processes, and the synthesis of heavy elements in the Universe.
the study of nuclear properties of neutron-rich nuclei.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the N=126 shell closure is robust against proton excitations, but that the N=82 shell closure is not robust against neutron excitations.
the Pt-204 nucleus exhibits a very complex level structure with a large number of excited states.
the N=126 shell closure is robust and is not significantly affected by proton-neutron interactions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the N = 126 shell is more robust against the presence of protons in the 1h(11/2) orbital than expected from the spherical shell-model calculation.
the structure of the nucleus Pt-204 can be understood within the framework of the spherical shell-model.
the N = 126 subshell is more robust than the Z = 82 subshell.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the N = 126 shell is not as robust as previously believed.
we have observed a new class of isomeric states in neutron-rich Pt-204.
the N = 126 neutron shell closure is weakened for the Pt-204 isotope, and this is in contrast to the behavior of the N = 184 isotone Pb-208.
